title: The Funnel That Runs While You Sleep
overview: Vishen Lakhiani told you the origin story of the masterclass, from a 2008 blog and Skype interviews to a model that has sold well over half a billion dollars, and then broke down exactly how a 60-minute masterclass teaches and sells at the same time. You learned the two things to lock in before you write a word (the core belief and the villain), the what-why-when-never-how rule, a minute-by-minute script structure, the Nine Agreements your script must secure, and the three-part skeleton to check every time: belief, villain, experience.
key_ideas: The email list is the most valuable asset an expert can build, more valuable than fans or a YouTube channel. In 2008 Vishen's blog Finer Minds captured emails with a free e-book; today your Instagram link in bio and your YouTube channel should do the same job. He was an enthusiast, not an expert, on a tiny niche (remote viewing), acting as the translation layer between the experts and ordinary readers, and that built the widest audience in the niche. The first masterclass was an hour-long Skype audio interview with an author: free, pointing people to the author's course, with a 50 per cent affiliate deal. That first interview generated 100,000 dollars for Vishen (200,000 in sales) and within 18 months he had done 980,000 dollars from audio interviews on a blog. Combining the interview format with the telesummit model for Burt Goldman's Quantum Jumping produced the first million-dollar launch; the programme still sells today. Even people who do not buy join the list, which is how the list grew to 2 million. It also shows there are two career paths: be the teacher, or be the host. Vishen was the host, not the teacher, from 2004 to 2014.

A masterclass teaches and sells at once by giving the what, the why and the when while inviting people to buy to get the how. It is 60 minutes: the first 45 educate, the last 15 sell. It is scripted word for word and read from a teleprompter, because randomness delays the sale and loses attention.

Lock in two things before writing. First, the core belief: people are not buying your product, they are buying a belief, and the whole masterclass shapes that one belief (for example, 'You don't manifest what you want, you manifest what you broadcast' for Regan Hillyer; 'Intuition is activated at the alpha level' for Silva; for a binaural-beats meditation product, 'Going into meditative states is not random; it can be enhanced with sound technology'). If someone could hold the belief and still not buy, it is the wrong belief. Depending on market sophistication, the belief usually includes your mechanism.

Second, the villain: never blame the user. If people fall asleep in meditation, the villain is social media training our brains for short attention spans; if people are addicted to sugar, the villain is big food putting sugar in around 70 per cent of grocery products (Vishen cited Dr Mark Hyman and a pro-sugar study funded by PepsiCo and Weight Watchers). It is empathetic and fact-based: 'It's not your fault, it's big food.'

Teach what, why and when, never how. For meditation: what it is, why it matters, when to do it (five minutes at night, six in the morning), but the audio technology, the countdown method and how to sit are in the paid programme. For a sugar-craving supplement: what it is, why it works, when to take it, with case studies, and the product is the how. In a 12-hour summit you can teach the how, and what you sell instead is the step-by-step application.

Every gift opens a gap in the same breath it closes one. Generosity without tension makes people satisfied, and satisfied people do not enrol; you want them grateful and hungry. Examples: the Quantum Jumping masterclass led people through a quantum jump for health and offered the collection (money, soulmate, sleep, ideal body) for 199 dollars; free samples of his Bliss supplement at events; cheese cubes on toothpicks in a supermarket. Tell them what you told them before you ask.

The centrepiece is a guided experience, and a before-and-after self-score makes the shift visible: score your energy 1 to 10, do a 15-minute Qigong technique, score again, then ask what 30 days could do. Vishen ran it live: how confident were you before the summit that you could build a million-dollar expert business in three years (many said 0 to 3) versus now on Day 3 (many said 6 to 10).

The Nine Agreements your script must secure, and an ask distribution map of no fewer than 25 requests and invitations through the class, framed as invitations, not pushy sales. For 'I need to act now', use a discount that only exists on that page (for example 50 dollars off that disappears if the page is closed) or genuine urgency around health, family or career, never fake urgency.

frameworks.name: What, Why, When, never How
steps: Teach the what: what the thing is, with scientific legitimacy and data.
Teach the why: why it works or why the problem matters.
Teach the when: when to apply it.
Never teach the how: the protocol, the breath count, the body scan, the technique. That is the programme they buy.

frameworks.name: Masterclass minute-by-minute breakdown
steps: Minutes 0 to 10: plant the belief, name the villain, make the promise.
Minutes 10 to 17: case studies and testimonials, ask for a commitment (put away your phone, give me your best attention), and spell out the cost of the problem.
Minutes 17 to 24: the paradigm shift, where you name your mechanism (for example active meditation versus clearing your mind) and make the first soft ask.
Then content and guided experience: the what, why and when, plus a short taste (a 7-minute version of a 22-minute meditation).
Minutes 36 to 46: the gift with a gap (tell them what you told them), the yes ladder (did you enjoy it? could this take you further? could you do this in 6 minutes a morning?), hint at the hole.
Then the sale: stack the value, state the price, give a fair guarantee, address objections (recordings, location), make the ask.

frameworks.name: The Nine Agreements
steps: The problem is serious enough to solve now.
What I have been doing cannot work.
The reason is something I did not know, so it is not my fault.
This person understands me better than I understand myself.
There is a different solution, and it has a name.
The specific solution is proven (case studies, testimonials).
I can see myself succeeding, and I am now allowed to hope (the guided experience and score increase).
Not doing this will cost me more than doing this.
I need to act now.

frameworks.name: Masterclass skeleton: three checks every time
steps: The belief: write down your core belief.
The villain: who or what you blame, never the user.
The experience: the guided experience that lets people feel the shift.

quotes.speaker: Vishen Lakhiani
quotes.text: The most valuable thing you can create as an expert is your email list. It is more valuable than your fans.

quotes.speaker: Vishen Lakhiani
quotes.text: Your masterclass doesn't cover multiple things, it shapes one belief. If they can hold a belief and still not buy, it's the wrong belief.

quotes.speaker: Vishen Lakhiani
quotes.text: Every gift opens a gap in the same breath, it closes one. This is the delicate dance between giving and asking.

quotes.speaker: Vishen Lakhiani
quotes.text: Generosity without tension makes people satisfied. Satisfied people do not enroll in your program. You want them grateful and hungry.

quotes.speaker: Vishen Lakhiani
quotes.text: You don't manifest what you want, you manifest what you broadcast. This is the core belief.

dialogue.speaker: Jason Goldberg
dialogue.text: Way before Oprah ever used the word masterclass, he was the guy who coined the term, all the way back in 2008. That single webinar did a million dollars in launch revenue from a blog, and since then he has sold roughly half a billion dollars through masterclasses alone. Vishen, take it away.

dialogue.speaker: Vishen Lakhiani
dialogue.text: One of the things Jason said is slightly incorrect. Oprah used the word masterclass first, for a TV show. I borrowed that word and used it for a webinar. I started calling my interviews masterclasses and I started refining it.

dialogue.speaker: Vishen Lakhiani
dialogue.text: Would you like to try this? If you have a masterclass, what is your core belief? Write it in the chat. You don't have to get it right now, we're going to go deeper. But one belief.

dialogue.speaker: Vishen Lakhiani
dialogue.text: No, because the villain is real. Social media, based on science, is causing people's attention spans to go down. In fact, it's empathetic. If you go to a therapist, is the therapist going to blame you? Nobody wants to be blamed.

dialogue.speaker: Vishen Lakhiani
dialogue.text: At the beginning of this summit, how confident did you feel that you could build an expert business doing a million in revenue in the next three years? Put a score in the chat. A lot of people are saying 0, 3, 1. Now, on Day 3, what is that score? Now it's going up to 6, 7, 8, and a lot of people are saying 10. If your score increased in just a few days of training, imagine what happens with four months.

exercises: Write your core belief in one sentence: the single belief someone must hold to buy from you. Test it: if they could hold this belief and still not buy, rewrite it.
Name your villain: the external cause of your customer's problem that is true, fact-based and lets you say 'it's not your fault'.
Design your guided experience and a before-and-after score (1 to 10) so people feel the shift inside the class.
Check your script against the Nine Agreements and count your invitations; aim for no fewer than 25 across the hour.
next_steps: Put an email sign-up on your Instagram link in bio and your YouTube channel this week, with a free e-book, meditation or lesson as the reason to join.
Draft the first 10 minutes of your masterclass: belief, villain, promise, using the minute-by-minute breakdown as your outline.
Decide whether you will be the teacher or the host, and if host, list three authors or experts you could interview for your first masterclass.
Sort your material into what, why and when (free) versus how (paid).
attribution_notes: Lines marked 'Mindvalley' at the start are the host Jason Goldberg introducing the session; every other line is Vishen Lakhiani. The audience question in the dialogue arrived via the chat and is given as Vishen reported it ('someone said, is this manipulative?'); the score exercise was also run through the chat, with Vishen reading the numbers aloud. Vishen mentioned that the full masterclass script and an AI that drafts it are part of the Mastery programme; details of that offer are not included here.
